features: aniline group, CYP3A4 cleared, dose 800 mg/day
outcome: Grade 3 liver injury in 4 of 38 patients within 6 weeks; patients over 70 affected 3 times as often.
change_that_worked: Start dose lowered to 400 mg; weekly liver tests for the first 8 weeks.

outcome: Patients also taking strong CYP3A4 inhibitors had 2.5 times higher drug levels and more liver toxicity.
change_that_worked: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors banned, with a 14-day washout before the first dose.

outcome: Atrial fibrillation in 7 percent, concentrated in patients over 65 with high blood pressure; major bleeding with warfarin.
change_that_worked: ECG at screening, Week 4 and Week 12; warfarin banned.

outcome: Rash in 9 percent and 1 case of Stevens-Johnson syndrome; 2 cases of haemolysis in G6PD-deficient patients.
change_that_worked: Excluded people with sulfa allergy; G6PD screening before dosing at sites in South Asia and Africa.

outcome: Infusion reactions in 12 percent at the first infusion.
change_that_worked: Antihistamine and steroid premedication, slower first infusion; reactions dropped to 2 percent.

outcome: QT prolongation over 20 ms at the top dose; 1 arrhythmia when combined with ondansetron.
change_that_worked: Dose capped, ECG at baseline and Day 7, QT-prolonging drugs banned, potassium checked before dosing.

outcome: Nausea and vomiting caused 18 percent of patients to drop out when the full dose was given from Week 1.
change_that_worked: Dose escalated over 8 weeks; dropouts fell to 6 percent.

outcome: Drug levels 70 percent higher when taken with a high-fat meal, causing more side effects in patients who ate before dosing.
change_that_worked: Protocol required fasting dosing; food-effect study added early.

outcome: All 6 participants dosed on the same morning had severe cytokine reactions within hours.
change_that_worked: Sentinel dosing with 48 hours between the first and the remaining participants, and a much lower start dose.
